name: pdk-relay-reply-records-dynamodb-rollout
instr:
# Reply-record storage rollout

## Goal
The team needs Relay to store reply records in DynamoDB with per-record expiry as the PostgreSQL reply table grows. Keep replies working while base-commit and upgraded email processors run side by side against the same PostgreSQL database and AWS services, and while historical rows are being copied.

## Requirements
1. Support `REPLY_STORAGE_PHASE=dual` and `REPLY_STORAGE_PHASE=dynamo` with `REPLY_DYNAMODB_TABLE` and optional `REPLY_DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT_URL`. The DynamoDB table uses a string `lookup` key matching the existing `Reply.lookup`. In `dual`, new forwards create both DynamoDB records and PostgreSQL rows readable by an unmodified processor; replies to old-processor forwards work through the upgraded processor, and both cross-version directions deliver to the original sender. In `dynamo`, new forwards create DynamoDB records but no PostgreSQL reply rows, and replies still deliver to their original sender.
2. Records have an `expires_at` epoch-seconds TTL attribute, based on their creation date (midnight UTC) plus `REPLY_TTL_DAYS` (default 90). Neither a DynamoDB record nor a PostgreSQL fallback past expiry may authorize a reply, even when DynamoDB has not swept it: such a reply returns HTTP 404 without sending email.
